name: Correct a payment that did not happen, or was recorded against the wrong person
priorityReason: A payment recorded against the wrong family leaves one household falsely settled and another falsely in debt, and neither is visible until somebody complains.

goal.capability: to put right a payment record that does not match what actually happened
goal.outcome: both households read correctly, and the books show what was entered as well as what was corrected

secondaryActors.involvement: Approves the correction. A payment record is not moved on one person's word.
Sees their account restored to the correct position.

additional.description: Reconciliation finds a recorded payment with no matching bank or gateway line.
A family disputes a receipt or a balance at the counter.

preconditions.condition: A payment has been recorded and is found not to match what actually happened (BR-2).

establishedBy.name: Recording a payment and issuing the receipt

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists. Raising requires Accounts; approving requires School Admin.
Where the payment belongs to another account, that account exists and has a charge to apply it to.

establishedBy.name: Issuing fee invoices at different scopes

preconditions.condition: A chart of accounts exists, so the reversing and re-recording entries can post.

establishedBy.name: Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals

postConditions: The payment has been reversed from the account it was wrongly recorded against, and that household's balance reads correctly again.
Where the money belongs to another household, it has been recorded there instead, and that household's balance reads correctly too.
Both entries stay visible. The original record is not deleted, so the books show what was entered as well as what was corrected.
The original receipt is marked superseded and a receipt has been issued to whoever actually paid.
The invoices on both sides have returned to their correct status, and any that is now unpaid is back in overdue tracking.
The correction carries what actually happened, who raised it and who approved it.
The correction is visible to reconciliation, so the bank line and the payment record can be matched properly.
Nothing about the charge has changed. Only the record of the payment was wrong.

businessRules.rule: A correction is raised by one person and approved by another. Moving a payment record between households is not something one hand does alone.
This use case corrects the record of a payment, not a charge. The charge itself is untouched, and where the charge is wrong the cancellation or credit route applies instead.
The correction states what was wrong: the payment never happened, it was recorded against the wrong student, the wrong household, the wrong invoice, or with the wrong amount or date.
A written account of what actually happened is mandatory. It is what somebody reads a year later when the entry is questioned.
Where the money belongs to another account, it is recorded there rather than simply removed. Reversing without re-recording leaves the school holding money nobody is credited with.
The original payment is marked reversed and stays visible. Nothing is deleted, so the books show what was entered as well as what was corrected.
Where the money merely moved between accounts, the school's cash total is unchanged. Only the household it belongs to changed, and reconciliation must still balance afterwards.
The original receipt is marked superseded rather than destroyed, and a receipt is issued to whoever actually paid. A family holding a receipt that no longer means anything must be able to see why.
Both invoices return to their correct status. Neither is edited, and an invoice that is now unpaid goes back into overdue tracking.
Where money was received but belongs to no charge, it is held as a household credit rather than left unattached.
A correction where the payment never happened reverses the entry entirely and records nothing in its place. That is the case reconciliation is most likely to find.
Corrections are visible in a report grouped by who raised them, because a pattern of corrections by one person is a control matter rather than a clerical one.
A correction cannot be raised against a payment already corrected. The current record is corrected instead.

transitions.condition: Approved. The reversal and any re-recording post together (BR-5, BR-6).
Returned with a reason. The record is untouched.

basicFlow.userAction: Finds a payment recorded in error, or recorded against the wrong student or household.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the payment, its receipt, the invoice it was applied to and how it was recorded.

basicFlow.userAction: Raises a correction stating what actually happened, and where the money belongs, the account it should be recorded against.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a written account, and refuses a correction that would leave the money unattached.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the correction and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval with who gave it and when.
Reverses the payment from the account it was wrongly recorded against. The original entry stays visible.
Records the payment against the correct account where it belongs there, so the money is never left uncredited.
Marks the original receipt superseded and issues a receipt to whoever actually paid.
Returns both invoices to their correct status, and puts any that is now unpaid back into overdue tracking.

alternateFlows.condition: The payment never happened at all
alternateFlows.navigation: Receipt log → Correct payment → Payment never happened
alternateFlows.behaviour: The entry is reversed entirely and nothing is recorded in its place. The invoice returns to unpaid and re-enters overdue tracking. This is the case reconciliation most often finds (BR-11).
alternateFlows.function: raisePaymentCorrection(paymentId, 'Payment never happened', description, null, null)

alternateFlows.condition: The money belongs to a sibling in the same household
alternateFlows.navigation: Correct payment → Correct student and invoice
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is re-recorded against the sibling's invoice. The household's total position is unchanged and only the child it sits against differs (BR-5).
alternateFlows.function: raisePaymentCorrection(paymentId, 'Recorded against the wrong student', description, siblingId, invoiceId)

alternateFlows.condition: The money belongs to no outstanding charge
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is held as a household credit rather than left unattached, and reaches the next invoice for that household (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not accept the correction
alternateFlows.navigation: Payment corrections → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason and the record is untouched in the meantime.

alternateFlows.condition: Reconciliation found a payment with no matching bank line
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Payment reconciliation → Correct payment
alternateFlows.behaviour: The correction is raised from the reconciliation screen, and the reconciliation picks up the corrected entry afterwards.

alternateFlows.condition: Only the amount or the date was wrong
alternateFlows.behaviour: The entry is reversed and re-recorded against the same account with the correct figure or date. The household does not change.
alternateFlows.function: raisePaymentCorrection(paymentId, 'Wrong amount recorded', description, sameStudentId, sameInvoiceId)

exceptions.condition: No account of what actually happened is given
exceptions.messageShown: Describe what actually happened. This is what somebody reads when the entry is questioned.

exceptions.condition: The correction would leave the money unattached
exceptions.systemResponse: It is refused. Money received is either credited to an account or held as a household credit (BR-5, BR-10).
exceptions.messageShown: Choose the account this payment belongs to, or hold it as a household credit.

exceptions.condition: Accounts attempt to approve their own correction
exceptions.messageShown: Only a School Admin can approve a payment correction.

exceptions.condition: The payment has already been corrected
exceptions.messageShown: This payment was corrected on 22-09-2026. Correct the current record instead.

exceptions.condition: The correct invoice named has no outstanding balance
exceptions.systemResponse: The payment cannot be applied to it, and the household credit route is offered instead.
exceptions.messageShown: That invoice is already settled. Hold the payment as a household credit, or choose another invoice.

exceptions.condition: The ledger posting fails part way
exceptions.systemResponse: The whole correction is rolled back. Neither account changes and the correction stays awaiting approval.
exceptions.messageShown: The correction could not be posted. Nothing has changed.

exceptions.condition: The charge is wrong rather than the payment record
exceptions.systemResponse: The correction is refused and the credit or cancellation route is named (BR-2).
exceptions.messageShown: The payment record is right and the charge is wrong. Raise a credit against the charge instead.

exceptions.condition: The receiving invoice was settled between raising and approving
exceptions.systemResponse: The payment is held as a household credit rather than forced onto a settled invoice.
exceptions.messageShown: That invoice was settled while this was awaiting approval. The payment is held as a household credit.

departures.requirement: Where money moves between accounts the school's cash total is unchanged, so reconciliation still balances after a correction.
The reversal, the re-recording, the receipt changes and both invoice status changes commit together or not at all. A half-applied correction would leave two households wrong instead of one.
The original payment and receipt are never deleted. Both the wrong entry and its correction stay visible.
Corrections are reported grouped by raiser, because a pattern by one person is a control matter rather than a clerical one.
Corrections and their postings are retained 7 years as financial records.

openQuestions.question: Is there a time limit after which a payment may no longer be corrected — a closed period or a closed session?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and a correction into a closed period changes a reported figure.

openQuestions.question: Should both households be told when a payment moves between them, or only the one that gains?
openQuestions.assumption: Both, since one household's balance worsens. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Is there a value above which the Principal rather than the School Admin should approve?
Where a correction restores an unpaid invoice that has passed its due date, does late fee accrue from the original due date or from the correction?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and charging a family for the school's clerical error would be wrong.

openQuestions.question: Who reviews the corrections report, and how often?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and BR-12 is the control that depends on it.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
